description: The Public Services Performance Tracker of the Institute for Government is an ongoing analysis of how public services in the United Kingdom, mainly England, are performing. The tracker page read on 2026-09-28 says it brings together more than 250 indicators on spending, demand, staffing and performance to examine the comparative and interconnected problems of services such as the NHS, schools, local government and criminal justice, that its main output is an annual report on nine services each autumn, and that shorter reports cover general practice, adult social care, prisons, educational outcomes and the children's social care market, with a local edition released on 30 April 2026; since 2024 it has been produced with the Nuffield Foundation. Coverage is national, with a local edition. Access is free to read; the licence of the indicators is not stated. Caveats: the indicators are compiled from official statistics, so the tracker is a secondary source, and the data behind charts may need to be requested or taken from the originals. It supports capacity planning and resilience studies of health, emergency and local services. Related record: data-rogs-emergency-services-fire-and-other-events is a comparable Australian government services report.
